items.description: The vocabulary every other item in this module imports: status enum, type enum, JSA phase enum, worker-role sets per permit type, the safety-range constant, and request/response models for the permit endpoints.
acceptance: EPermitStatus: DRAFT | PENDING | REJECTED | ACTIVE | FIRE_MONITOR | CLOSED | EXPIRED

EJsaPhase: pre | process | post
A single exported SAFETY_RANGES constant encoding LEL=0, O2 19.5-23.5, CO<=50 (confined), wind<=25 (heights), and which readings each type requires
A pure validateReadings(type, readings, outdoorWork) helper returning the list of failing readings — unit tested at the boundaries: 0, 19.4, 19.5, 23.5, 23.6, 50, 50.1, 25, 25.1
Worker-role option sets per type (confined: Entrant/Attendant/Gas Tester; hot: Fire Watcher/Operator/Helper; heights: per design)

items.description: The 6-step container: stepper header, per-step validation gate on Next, Back navigation, and draft persistence to the API. Step bodies land in PMT-005..009.
acceptance: 6-node stepper with done / current / upcoming states and connecting rules
Next is blocked while the current step's schema fails; the blocked reason is shown next to the button
Back never validates
Step 6 replaces Next with a green Submit button
Draft state persists via POST /permits then PATCH /permits/:id — not localStorage
Wizard state lives in a page-scoped composable (useWizard), not a Pinia store

items.notes: Design lines 146-165 (stepper) and 417-425 (footer). || DONE. Step registry WIZARD_STEPS: IWizardStepDef[] = {key, labelKey, component, schema} — StepperHeader, WizardFooter and useWizard all derive from it, so filling a step means editing only that step .vue + .schema.ts. useWizard(steps) takes an injectable array so tests can exercise gating (the real placeholder schemas always pass). CREATE-THEN-PATCH RACE solved with a single inflight promise chain: doPersist() reads draftId at execution time, not call time, so a second write queues behind the first and never fires a second create — covered by a deferred-promise test. Nothing POSTs until formData.type is set. goToStep re-validates EVERY prior step, not just an unlocked index — otherwise editing an earlier step back into an invalid state would let the stepper jump past it (invisible today, live from PMT-005). 375px: compact Step X of N + progress bar below sm, full 6-node stepper at sm+. items.name: Draft resume, edit and Duplicate & Edit
items.description: A DRAFT permit cannot currently be reopened and a REJECTED one cannot be re-used: Permit.router.ts is list/create/detail only, so PMT-010's 'Edit Permit' and 'Duplicate & Edit' banner CTAs ship disabled. Add the route(s), hydrate the wizard from an existing permit, and wire both CTAs.
acceptance: A route exists that opens the wizard against an existing permit id; PMT-010's DRAFT 'Edit Permit' CTA is enabled and navigates to it
useWizard hydrates formData from the fetched permit (including safetyReading, workers, jsaSteps, photos) and sets draftId, so the first edit PATCHes instead of creating a second draft
Resume lands the user on the first step that does not validate, not always step 1; every earlier step is left unlocked
Only an editable permit can be opened this way — a non-DRAFT id renders the server's PERMIT_NOT_EDITABLE verdict rather than a broken wizard, and the client does not pre-empt that check

REJECTED 'Duplicate & Edit' copies the rejected permit into a NEW draft and opens it. There is no duplicate/clone route on the wire (openapi.json has no such path) — it is a client-side POST /permits followed by PATCH, and the copy must NOT carry over id, status, submittedAt, rejectedReason/rejectedAt or any approval/closure field
The safetyReading log is not replayed on duplicate — safetyReading APPENDS a row per PATCH (see useWizard's lastPersistedReading), so a copied reading must be sent at most once
Leaving and re-entering an unfinished resumed draft does not create additional drafts
./init.sh green
items.notes: AGENTS.md records a deliberate decision that wizard state lives in a composable, not a Pinia store, so navigating to /permits/create always starts clean. That rule is about the CREATE route and must stay true; hydration belongs to the resume route, which is a different entry point. Do not convert useWizard to a store. Unblocks the two acceptance sub-clauses PMT-010 shipped disabled.
